subject: biology

hotspots.label: Cell wall
hotspots.description: A firm outer layer that gives the bacterium its shape and support.
hotspots.positionHint: A thin outer sleeve around the rod-shaped cell.

hotspots.label: Cell membrane
hotspots.description: A thin inner layer just under the wall that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
hotspots.positionHint: A pale line right inside the cell wall.
hotspots.function: Controls what passes in and out.

hotspots.label: DNA (genetic material)
hotspots.description: The bacterium's loose DNA, floating freely since it has no nucleus.
hotspots.positionHint: A coil/loose knot of DNA near the center of the cell interior.
hotspots.function: Carries the instructions the bacterium needs.

hotspots.label: Flagellum
hotspots.description: A tail-like whip that the bacterium can use to move.
hotspots.positionHint: A long thin tail extending from one end of the cell.

hotspots.label: Cells splitting
hotspots.description: The place where the bacterium pinches to split in two during binary fission.
hotspots.positionHint: The pinching midline seen during the division animation.
hotspots.function: The split that makes two cells from one.

visualStyleNotes: Anatomy Atelier best throughout: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial glow, no floor grid, no props and minimal, clean surface so the microbe is a calm, centered subject. Stylized-clean clear primitive bacteria, soft neutral material, not glowing or gamey. Strong saturated color reserved for the hotspot dots.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0, matte roughness ~0.55-0.65. DNA coil is a clean stylized knot, not glowing.
assetBrief: SUBJECT: a single rod-shaped bacterium, centered and large, with a partial cutaway exposing a membrane, a loose DNA coil, and a trailing flagellum. A division layer animates the cell pinching into two. Muted warm backdrop, soft neutrals. Named nodes: BacteriumBody, CellWall, CellMembrane, DNA, Flagellum, SplitPoint. Budget 10-14k.
